title: Implement Custom Promise.allSettled
problemStatement: Implement `myPromiseAllSettled(promises)` without using native `Promise.allSettled`. It takes an iterable of promises (or non-promise values) and returns a promise that resolves with an array of objects `{ status: 'fulfilled', value }` or `{ status: 'rejected', reason }` after ALL promises settle.
interviewTrap: Using `Promise.all` which short-circuits on the first rejection. `allSettled` must wait for every promise regardless of success or failure.

testCases.name: Handles mix of resolved and rejected promises
Preserves exact order of input results
testCases.testFn: const p1 = new Promise(r => setTimeout(() => r('slow'), 30)); const p2 = new Promise(r => setTimeout(() => r('fast'), 5)); const res = await myPromiseAllSettled([p1, p2]); return res.map(r => r.value);

details.name: Handles mix of resolved and rejected promises
Preserves exact order of input results

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Implementing `Promise.allSettled` requires waiting for all promises in an iterable to settle (either fulfill or reject), returning an array of settlement descriptor objects in original order: `{ status: 'fulfilled', value }` or `{ status: 'rejected', reason }`.
stepByStepWalkthrough: Convert input iterable to an array `promises = Array.from(iterable)`.
If the array is empty, immediately resolve with `[]`.
Initialize an array `results = new Array(promises.length)` and `settledCount = 0`.
Iterate over promises with index `i`: wrap with `Promise.resolve(promises[i])` to handle non-promise values.
Attach `.then(value => { results[i] = { status: 'fulfilled', value }; checkDone(); }, reason => { results[i] = { status: 'rejected', reason }; checkDone(); })`.
In `checkDone()`, increment `settledCount++`. If `settledCount === promises.length`, resolve outer promise with `results`.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: Unlike `Promise.all` which fast-fails on the first rejection, `Promise.allSettled` never rejects. Results must maintain input indexing order even if promise 3 settles before promise 1.

complexity.time: O(N) where N is the number of promises.

edgeCasesHandled: Empty iterable resolves immediately with empty array.
Mix of fulfilled and rejected promises completes without short-circuiting.
Mix of raw values (primitives) and Promises handled safely via `Promise.resolve()`.
Preserves exact input order regardless of resolution timing.

specifications: TC39 Proposal for Promise.allSettled (Championed by Mathias Bynens)
verifiedRules: Result objects adhere strictly to { status: 'fulfilled', value } and { status: 'rejected', reason } shapes.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does Promise.allSettled differ from Promise.all in failure scenarios?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: `Promise.all` fast-fails: if any single promise rejects, the returned promise immediately rejects with that error, ignoring all other pending or resolved promises. In contrast, `Promise.allSettled` NEVER rejects; it waits for every single promise to settle and returns an array of descriptors: `{ status: 'fulfilled', value }` or `{ status: 'rejected', reason }`.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How do you ensure results in a custom allSettled maintain input order?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: By pre-allocating an array of the exact input length (`const results = new Array(promises.length)`) and populating each index `i` when that specific promise resolves (`results[i] = descriptor`). A separate counter tracks `settledCount++`. When `settledCount === promises.length`, the outer promise resolves with `results`.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests understanding of async ordering and array index stability.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is the difference between Promise.any and Promise.race?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: `Promise.race` settles with the FIRST promise to settle (whether fulfilled OR rejected). `Promise.any` ignores rejections and settles with the FIRST FULFILLED promise. It only rejects if ALL input promises reject, throwing an `AggregateError`.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Checks knowledge of all 4 ES2020/ES2021 Promise combinators (all, race, allSettled, any).

realWorldUseCases.description: Sending 10,000 notifications in parallel: failure to deliver to 5 users should not abort or obscure successful delivery to the other 9,995 users.
A dashboard fetching metrics from 5 independent microservices renders partial widgets for services that succeeded while displaying retry buttons for failed widgets.
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: const [cpu, mem, disk] = await Promise.allSettled([getCpu(), getMem(), getDisk()]);

howToExplain.opening: Promise.allSettled is a concurrency combinator that guarantees complete outcome tracking by awaiting all promises without short-circuiting on failure.
keyPoints: Never rejects; always fulfills with an array of outcome descriptors.
Each outcome conforms strictly to { status: 'fulfilled', value } or { status: 'rejected', reason }.
Preserves exact input order even when promises settle out of order.
Essential for batch operations where partial success is acceptable.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Using allSettled instead of all prevents one failing non-critical request from crashing an entire page.
analogies: A teacher grading exams: they don't stop grading the whole class just because one student failed; they grade everyone and hand back the full report card.

commonMistakes.mistake: Pushing results into an array using array.push() on completion.
commonMistakes.why: Pushing as promises resolve scrambles the order: a fast 10ms promise will appear before a slow 100ms promise regardless of their original array order.

followUpDeepDive.question: What is an AggregateError and which Promise combinator throws it?
followUpDeepDive.answer: Introduced in ES2021 alongside `Promise.any`, `AggregateError` is a native error subclass that wraps multiple individual errors into an `.errors` array property when all promises passed to `Promise.any` reject.
